K1.stone_why: Faceted, polygonal bowls on bold text, numbers and capitals give a clear hewn-stone feel without losing the serif base.
K1.carving_why: Facets are applied consistently across lowercase, capitals and digits, and 0/O, 1/7, 3/8 stay distinct, though the heaviest bold counters look slightly lumpy.
K1.calm_why: Steady, well-weighted presence; the heavy ss01 SISIFO is assertive but not shouting.
K1.personality_why: The chiselled polygon curves give a recognisable voice on top of a familiar book serif.
K1.inscription_why: ss01 capitals are wide with round O C and narrower E S, giving a dignified inscriptional rhythm, but serifs stay bookish rather than Roman-cut.

K2.stone_why: Same faceted, hewn treatment as K1, so bold display reads as cut stone.
K2.carving_why: Cuts are coherent across cases and digits stay distinct, though the condensed ss01 capitals compress the facets into tighter, busier shapes.
K2.calm_why: Composed and readable; the condensed capitals feel a little tense but not aggressive.
K2.personality_why: Distinct carved voice, with the tall condensed capitals adding an upright, slightly Germanic note.
K2.inscription_why: ss01 capitals are condensed with narrow O and C, the opposite of classical Roman proportions.

K3.stone_why: Trajan-like flared capitals hint at inscription, but strokes are smooth and calligraphic, with no hewn quality.
K3.carving_why: No visible carving facets; the ss01 block adds swash ligatures instead.
K3.calm_why: Elegant but fussy: swashes, odd ligatures and an all-small-caps body draw attention to themselves and read less steadily.
K3.personality_why: Strongly flavoured and recognisable, but it is a borrowed classical-display look rather than a voice of its own.
K3.inscription_why: The base capitals are Roman-proportioned, but the ss01 swashes and interlocking LI/BR ligatures turn it decorative rather than cut-in-stone.

K4.stone_why: Faceted bold and numbers plus flared, wedge-serifed ss01 capitals read clearly as inscription in stone.
K4.carving_why: Cuts are crisp and digits distinct; the flared ss01 capitals are a slightly different idiom from the faceted lowercase, but they still belong together.
K4.calm_why: Calm, dignified presence; the lighter ss01 weight keeps the capitals from shouting.
K4.personality_why: Carved lowercase combined with glyphic flared capitals and the long Q tail make it memorable.
K4.inscription_why: Wide round O C, narrow E S R, flared glyphic terminals and an even rhythm give the most convincing Roman inscriptional capitals of the set.

K5.stone_why: A clean, smooth book serif; solid, but nothing reads as carved or hewn.
K5.carving_why: No visible carving at any size.
K5.calm_why: Very calm and steady with adequate presence, though a little plain for display.
K5.personality_why: A competent but anonymous text serif.
K5.inscription_why: ss01 capitals are condensed with narrow O and C, a newspaper rhythm rather than Roman inscription.
